elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 2(a): "TrueLink hereby grants to Client and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates a non-exclusive license to use the Interface ... in the ordinary course of their business" (the plural "their" conforms the use-scope to the added affiliates). Coverage is conditioned on written notice rather than automatic, which is the fallback formulation, but the grant does extend to affiliates.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither the amended Section 2(a) grant nor Section 2(b) scope names contractors, subcontractors or service providers acting for Client. The cited Section 8(c) "officers, employees, and agents" language is an access-restriction obligation on Client, not a grant of use rights, and it is not part of the rendered operative text. To reach preferred, insert "and contractors acting on its behalf" into the Section 2(a) grant.

Condition does not apply: there is no paid-up licence here. Section 2(c) states "The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12," i.e. a term licence tied to the Agreement, with no one-time paid-up fee in the cited grant/term provisions.

Condition does not apply for the same reason: the licence is a term licence running "until this Agreement is terminated" (Section 2(c)), not a paid-up licence. Separately, the grant contains no "revocable" or at-will revocation language, so nothing in the rendered text lets TrueLink pull the licence at discretion.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Section 2(c) ties licence duration to termination "in accordance with section 12," and Section 12 is neither cited nor rendered, so the available termination triggers (convenience, expiry, breach) cannot be confirmed. The redline adds no limitation on the grounds for ending the licence; to secure this element the drafter must either amend Section 2(c) to survive except on termination for Client's uncured material breach, or constrain Section 12.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 15 carve-out: "except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, in the case of Client, to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction." Scoped to M&A successors rather than successors generally, which is a preferred-wording shortfall only; the existing affiliate carve-out is retained.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 2(a) grants the licence to "Client and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates," with the use-scope pluralised to "their business." The trigger (written notice to TrueLink) is self-executing and requires no TrueLink consent.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 15 removes the consent requirement for a Client assignment "to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction," curing the original bar that permitted only assignment to "a financially responsible affiliate." Rights "under this Agreement" include the Section 2 licence, so the licence follows Client into an M&A transaction.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language — affiliates added to the Section 2(a) grant on written notice, and an M&A successor carve-out added to the Section 15 consent requirement. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation because the original text failed both fallback elements (grant ran to "Client" alone; Section 15 barred transfer with only a financially-responsible-affiliate carve-out).

Preferred level is not complete: the grant still omits contractors acting on Client's behalf. If the preferred position is pursued, insert "and contractors acting on its behalf" after the affiliate language in Section 2(a); the Section 8(c) "agents" reference is an access-control obligation and does not operate as a grant.

Preferred is also unverifiable on subscription termination: Section 2(c) hands the licence's life to an unrendered Section 12, so termination grounds cannot be confirmed. This is not a defect in the chosen fallback target, but it is the second gap to close if preferred is later sought.

Minimality holds: only two surgical edits, plus the necessary "its business" to "their business" conforming change. Favourable existing language is preserved (the "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out, Client's freedom to use alternative systems, the Section 2(c) term), no operative term is duplicated, and no obligation outside the fallback checklist is added.

Intent is preserved: the Section 15 carve-out is drafted one-way ("in the case of Client"), which is favourable to us and creates no reciprocal obligation; fees, term, scope of rights in Section 2(b) and termination mechanics are untouched and non-contradictory.

Minor drafting note (not a defect): "affiliates" is used lowercase and undefined, consistent with existing Section 15 usage; if a defined "Affiliate" term exists elsewhere, conform capitalisation for consistency.
The margin comment accurately describes the two operations and cites the playbook position without over-claiming; no element is left merely promised in the comment.
